cues.text: A computer can only calculate with numbers.
So every NLP method starts the same way: it turns text into numbers.
The methods differ in one thing: what they keep, and what they lose.
The simplest way is a bag of words. We just count each word.
Dog bites man. One dog, one bites, one man.
Now: man bites dog. The counts are exactly the same.
So a bag of words loses the word order. Two different stories get the same numbers.
A better idea: give every word a point in space, a vector.
Words with similar meaning land close together. Good sits near great. Bad is far away.
This is an embedding, like Word2Vec.
But it is static. Bank gets the same point in river bank and in bank loan.
Contextual models, like BERT, fix this.
They read the whole sentence, and give each bank its own vector.
The price: they are big, slow and expensive.
For the exam, remember three things.
Bag of words loses the order.
Embeddings put similar words close, but one word has one vector.
And a big model is not always the right tool. For a simple task like spam, try a cheap model first.
